workflow_runs.display_title: feat(proj): global default_model + ^d to set it in the model picker

head_commit.message:
feat(proj): global default_model + ^d to set it in the model picker

The model picker's default was hardwired to index 0 of the menu, which for
pi is whatever claude-bridge model pi --list-models happens to print first
(claude-fable-5). Add a top-level default_model config key honored as the
picker's initial selection (per-project pin still wins, else global, else
first entry), and a ^d keybinding in the model overlay that sets the
highlighted model as that global default: it selects it, persists to
config.toml via a comment-preserving upsert, marks it with a star, and
confirms in the footer.

head_commit.message:
creel: --event-file writes a value-free {name,dest,action} record on save

So a keybind or harness watcher can tell an agent WHAT was captured (env-var name + dest + action), never the value. Only a real save (added/updated) emits an event; cancel/error write nothing.

workflow_runs.display_title: proj: model selection in the new-work picker

head_commit.message:
proj: model selection in the new-work picker

Mirror agent selection with a per-agent model choice. While naming new work,
Tab cycles the agent and Shift-Tab opens a filterable list of that agent's
models (type to filter, arrows to move, enter to pick, esc to keep the
current). Changing the agent re-seeds the model to its default. The choice
rides out in Result.Model and is woven into the launch as `claude --model <id>
…` / `pi --model <provider/id> …` (empty model → agent's own default;
cursor/none ignore it).

Model menus are per-agent: claude's is a built-in Anthropic list (Claude Code
can't enumerate its models), pi's is discovered from `pi --list-models`,
filtered to the providers named under [model_providers] in config.toml and
cached ~24h at ~/.cache/proj/pi-models.txt. A per-project default_model pins a
project's model (honoured on the interactive path and the proj new path; no
CLI flag).

Threads a model arg through EnsureSession/agentLaunchCmd; the model overlay
reuses the picker's filter/window machinery and an injected models resolver so
tests never shell out to pi.

workflow_runs.display_title: proj: test agentLaunchCmd + roots negative cases

head_commit.message:
proj: test agentLaunchCmd + roots negative cases

agentLaunchCmd is the sole home of the pane launch shape (claude --name '<n>'
--, with the load-bearing trailing -- that keeps a bare claude out of agent
view). It had no coverage; the zsh guard that used to protect it referenced a
helper removed when launch moved into this binary. Add session_launch_test.go
guarding the --, --name, shell-quoting, and missing-bin degradation, and fix
the doc comment that still pointed at the retired zsh helpers.

Also port the roots negative/exclusion cases from the retired zsh proj-roots
test: a dir under no root has no name, a root dir is not itself a project,
unknown names do not resolve, and a root at a non-existent dir is dropped.

workflow_runs.name: verify
workflow_runs.display_title: feat(proj): add --json and --command to proj new (hail family stream)

head_commit.message:
feat(proj): add --json and --command to proj new for hail

The hail bridge needs to spawn a task into the correct per-project tmux
server with a given command as the pane program, and needs the result as
data. proj new gains:

- --json: prints one object {name,project,work,socket,dir,pane,created}
  and nothing else on stdout; errors unchanged on stderr. socket is the
  tmux -L value (proj-<project>); pane is the working pane's #{pane_id};
  created is false when the session was reused.
- --command <argv>: runs argv directly in the working pane via
  respawn-pane -k -c dir -- argv (no shell, no send-keys). Everything
  after --command (or --) is the verbatim argv. With --agent it records
  the agent in a new @proj_agent user option that proj list prefers over
  pane process detection. Against a reused session --command is not
  applied (exit 3, 'session exists; --command ignored'); the --json
  object with created:false is still printed so hail can detect reuse.

EnsureSession gains a command []string param and returns created bool;
a runner/newSessionHome seam makes its tmux calls unit-testable. Both
proj contracts hold: cmdNew still never calls Goto (detached), and the
command rides the existing respawn-pane -c dir call so #{session_path}
stays $HOME.

Skill + man/usage updated. Spec: hail-family-design.md §1.

workflow_runs.name: release
workflow_runs.display_title: fix(proj): scrub tmux target separators from session names (#20)

head_commit.message:
fix(proj): scrub tmux target separators from session names (#20)

A '.' or ':' in a session name makes it unaddressable by the "=name"
exact-match target (tmux parses target as session:window.pane), so
has-session misses an existing dotted session and EnsureSession then
errors "duplicate session" on resume. Work names already exclude both,
but project names come from dir basenames (e.g. ".claude"), so scrub the
composed name in SessionName. muster keys identity off the socket and the
@claude_task label, not this string, so mail mapping is unaffected.

head_commit.message:
refactor(proj,creel): move CLI command impls into internal packages (#18)

Move cmd/proj's dispatch, subcommands, and picker/sidebar-spawn logic into
internal/projcli, and cmd/creel's dispatch/parseArgs into internal/creel,
leaving each cmd/<tool>/main.go a thin os.Exit(<tool>.Dispatch(os.Args[1:],
os.Stdout, os.Stderr)) shim per the family layout convention.

proj's CLI logic could not move into the existing internal/proj package
(the tmux/session/roots domain layer) because internal/projtui already
imports internal/proj, and the moved main.go imports internal/projtui —
merging would have created an import cycle. It lives in the new
internal/projcli package instead, importing both internal/proj and
internal/projtui as before. creel had no such conflict and folds
directly into its existing internal/creel package.

Pure move + repackage: Dispatch preserves run()'s exact exit-code
semantics and stdout/stderr routing at the dispatch level; command Run
internals, the bare-project/picker routes, and cmd/scratch (still
package main) are untouched. Verified byte-identical CLI behavior
(help/version/commands/man/list/current/new/bogus flags/status-file)
against the pre-refactor binaries.

head_commit.message:
cli: man/commands coverage for proj+scratch; creel v0.3.0 check

creel registers no subcommands of its own, but its pre-Dispatch switch was
missing "man"/"commands" from the routed list, leaving tools.New's
auto-registered man/commands built-ins unreachable (they fell into
parseArgs as a positional name instead). Fixed with a one-line switch
addition — parseArgs itself is untouched.

The identical gap existed in proj's pre-Dispatch switch: "man"/"commands"
fell into the open-project fallback instead of Dispatch, which would try
to launch the picker TUI against a "project" literally named man/commands.
Fixed the same way so `proj man` / `proj commands --json` work per the
final gate.

Added coverage tests (mirroring kempt's) asserting `commands --json`
parses and lists every registered command for proj and scratch, and that
`man` renders the .TH header; creel gets a man-only coverage test since it
registers no commands of its own.

Folded in two deferred Task 3 scratch cleanups: dropped the unused
initialPath parameter from cmdPath/cmdPrint/cmdAppend (each already
recomputes path from cwd internally), and collapsed run()'s switch whose
case/default bodies were identical Dispatch calls into one unconditional
return.

head_commit.message:
feat(proj): picker UX overhaul — roots mgmt, reap, scope toggle, polish (#16)

Filtering & keys
- Any printable rune now starts a filter; commands moved to ctrl chords, so
  search terms can begin with s/a/x/q.

Roots management (previously stubbed)
- ^a add a root inline (validated dir, appended to ~/.config/proj/roots).
- ^e edit the roots file in $EDITOR, reloading on return.

Reap
- ^x kills the highlighted session with a two-step confirm; refuses non-session
  rows and the session hosting the picker. esc cancels without exiting.

Entrance scope
- Two-way scope toggle on tab (Folders default ⇄ Sessions); dropped the
  synthetic "home base" row.

New-session settings
- Agent + sidebar are now set only in the "+ new work…" input (tab agent,
  ^s sidebar), not while browsing/jumping where they don't apply.

TUI polish
- Alt-screen + mouse-wheel; responsive bordered preview pane; onboarding
  empty states; bubbles/help footer (? for full legend); mauve selection accent.

head_commit.message:
feat(creel): masked secret capture into a local .env

New tackle tool: a tmux-popup masked-input TUI (dest -> key name -> value,
with a folder picker) that upserts KEY=value into a .env, chmod 600 + gitignore.
The captured value never leaves the process; harness callers get only a status
token via --status-file.

head_commit.message:
fix(proj): quote the =name tmux target so zsh EQUALS expansion can't eat it (#14)

proj session names are project/work (e.g. tools-workspace/proj). The
print (outside-tmux, eval'd by the zsh shim) and detach -E (cross-server,
run by tmux default-shell=/bin/zsh) paths emitted an unquoted -t =<name>.
A leading unquoted = triggers zsh EQUALS expansion (=word -> path of
command word), which aborts with '<name> not found' before tmux ever runs.

Symptoms: outside tmux, jump/create failed with '(eval):1: ... not found'
and no attach; inside tmux, a cross-server jump detached the client first
(pulling the user out of pi) then failed the reattach the same way.

Single-quote the target with = inside the quotes. switch-client stays a
direct exec.Command arg (no shell), so it's left unquoted.
